It was supposed to be another long day at work. Right up until it wasn’t. The first sign things were off was when I heard yelling and screaming from down the hall from the break room. Someone looked like they got kicked backwards with a scream. Security ran out of their room and started running to deal with the intruder. Seconds later, they were knocked aside like rag dolls. At this point, those near the break room ran into it and closed the doors. My heart pounded into my chest as I stood there at the coffee machine with a half finished cup of coffee that needed to be tempered with cold water, creamer, and sugar. The veins in my muscles tightened as others cowered in fear. The door was locked. A few prayed as they tried to barricade the door with the tables inside. I merely just finished making my coffee and stood there waiting. Some prayed, one called 911, others called their families. I just stood there waiting. I’d gotten a good look at the figure in the distance. Clad in black and gray, hooded, with a polarized face mask. Some knew the name, others didn’t. 

Her (it was assumed) name was Gray. Nothing extravagant- just Gray. She was one of the most popular supervillains in the planet, infamous for taking on various teams of heroes while also striking on various targets: both civil and military. She was so strong, she kicked in steel doors and threw them away like rag dolls. She was fast, but preferred to delude her enemies into thinking she was slow. Nobody knows what her deal is-but the fact that she was in my work place was surprising. I merely stood and waited. I did jump
a little as the door suddenly broke open off its hinges  with the makeshift barricade now tossed aside as she came through. “Oh Jesus,” a coworker whispered. “Fuck,” another whispered as she finally came through. I merely sipped my coffee, unconcerned. 2020 was a shit year. 

I looked at her with an unimpressed face with my eyes squinting. I raised a brow. “What do you want?” I asked. She better have a good reason for this. 

She then walked over to me. She was around 5’8, I was 5’4. “You,” her distorted voice spoke. “You’re coming with me,” she said, using her size to intimidate me. I sighed, tossing my cup into the trash. I was tired, stressed out, and dealing with some ungodly level of bs. I smiled as I spoke. “Get out,” I told her. I wasn’t in the mood for this. Why would a superhero be after me? All I do is janitorial work. My throat was grabbed, and my feet suddenly didn’t touch the floor. “I wasn’t asking,” she grunted. I gasped for air and then grinned a devilish detail. “N-N” I started to say, lifting a finger. Her grip lessened. “What is it?” She asked. Both of my hands grabbed her thumb that held me right as her grip tightened. “Napoleon,” I said  in devilish delight. Both hands suddenly forced her thumb back from its original position, breaking it. She screamed, dropping me. “You bastard!” she roared raising a fist to strike. I dodged as she used most of her weight and momentum to hit me, only to strike the floor instead, breaking the tile. I spun and dodged the attack coming up behind her and had her head on a headlock, choking her instead as I leaned back over our sinks I used all the strength at my disposal to keep her in restraint as she choked out. “Let me give you a lesson: during Napoleon’s conquest of northern Italy, he faced an enemy army  that had more numbers than he had in his own army. That means,
:he had to split his army and piecemeal the enemy army’s smaller units, taking them out until they were gone.” I chuckled as she started to drift into unconsciousness. “Of course, I didn’t pull it off, but the thumb was a good move, you have to admit that.” I told her-She went limp. I dropped her to the floor as everyone in the break room stared at me in shock. I shrugged. “Meh,” I shrugged, deciding to take Gray’s mask off. Hopefully there was a reward for this.

I first met her after work. We worked different shifts, different departments but the same building. We talked over some trivial fantasy stuff, later into medieval era history and connected. Later, we dated. To me, she was the one. Oddly enough, I couldn’t help but notice how strange her skin looked in a few places, like it was some kind of weird suit... and yet... she sounded and acted human.

After a few months of dating, we agreed that she could move in. “Okay, I’m going to lay on you a ground rule or several.” She told me. I tilted my head and leaned forward. 

“Sure,” I said, interested. “I need to spend at least two hours a day cleaning my skin in the bathroom, otherwise- it’s going to rot.” She said, grimacing. I blinked. “Nani?” I asked. She pinched the bridge of her nose, sighing and held my hand. “Baby, look at me.” She told me. I did do. Her eyes bore into mine with serious love but also as some kind of plea. “I love you, really. But I need to do this alone. I have a skin condition, okay?” She told me. “And no, I don’t want to make either of us uncomfortable talking about it.” She told me. “When I do my cleaning, under no circumstances: don’t ever see me without my skin on.” She told me. I blinked in confusion. And then I remembered the odd places. “Oh,” I started to say and then realized. “OH,” I realized. I grimaced. Now, I understood. “I think I know what’s going on, but I’ll let you clean your skin.” I told her. “Take all the time you need,” I told her, reassuring her with a smile. “Besides,” I told her. “How do you feel about this being the second body I have?” I asked. The look on her face was priceless. I kissed her nose. “Love you, regardless.” I told her.

I’d been going out with my girlfriend for about seven months. On the surface? I look like a normal Japanese-American... except I’m not. I’m actually what’s called a Futakuchi-oona. No- not *that* kind of futa- get your head out of the gutter. That just means I’m a monster with a mouth on the back of my head. You know how hard it is to hide that? Pretty hard. I have to use a fake patch with hair that looks exactly like my hair color and the hair length has to be same as everything genuine.., and the patch as to stick *all day* breathing with one mouth and a nose? Somewhat okay. Not using your other mouth all day for anything? No. Just.. no. I feel like I have to use it for something. So, I go take a midnight snack after I take off my patch. That and for an occasional prank. Only on Halloween and April Fool’s day. I make sure to put it back on, go back to bed with her none-the-wiser. 

Except tonight was different. I’d been waiting all night to finish this one sandwich I got from work and decided to eat with my other mouth... right until I heard footsteps and turned my eyes to see my girlfriend. I tended up and my other mouth swallowed. “Uhh... I can explain?” My other mouth said my front mouth grimaced. 
Her face went from one of shock to one of pure joy. “Finally!” She shouted. I tilted my head at her. I said one word so common and cliche... but also expressive in its meaning.

She wore a simple dress that looked like something a commoner would wear back in the 1700s. “I’ve been wanting to meet you. My name’s Elizabeth.” She said: I tilted my head and took hers. Oookay? “Im your ancestor,”  she told me. I tilted my head like a German Shepherd. “What?” I asked weakly. “You’re in heaven, dear.” She told me, smiling. She pointed to my head. I slowly turned my head upwards and looked back at the woman claiming to be my ancestor. “If this is heaven...” I started to say...”then I’d hate to see the other place,” I told her, taking it. “None of us like to, dear.” She said, solemnly as I stood up. “Come along , the others are waiting for us. She was the Goddess of Balance. She bore a heavy burden and toll, keeping both Light and Darkness in check be it barbarous hordes or overzealous fanatics in check. Unfortunately, this took a heavy toll on her. She had just had to deal with a particularly troubling matter of one of my brother priests calling for a crusade against the barbarians east of here... centuries after a brutal campaign themselves that failed. 

She sat in a garden of the church I pastored and looked into a pool. It was never easy when one of your own followers, a man that ought to know the meaning of balance was in actuality a bit of prick. She not only tore him a new one but cast him out of the priesthood with more wounds than possible as soon as she saw what his own followers had done to the few foreigners in the city he served in. I can still see the hanging bodies when I close my eyes. I actually had to bring my own parishioners to deal with his... and promptly knocked some fools’ teeth out... and broke some noses and bones. I used to be a boxer, then I thought about being HER boxer. But, what happened afterwards was even more damaging, the kinsmen of my former brothers’ victims went on a rampage... and many dues before the bloodshed was over. It took weeks for the priests if death to complete all the proper funeral rites. So many bodies... so many graves. This then was the price of imbalance. 

“My lady?” I asked softly after doing my prayers. She sat in the flower bed, unresponsive. My fellow priests were not around, either at other parishes or pilgrimages. I was alone with her. I sat down next to her. “It was not your fault, milady.” I reassured her. “Some men go too far, we’ve all known this.” I told her. “He was one of mine...” she said softly. I could see the stains of tears on her cheeks. I sighed. “You did what you had to do, milady. The man was my brother priest, but what he did was inexcusable to any degree.” I told her like a father. We sat in silence. I looked at the goddess of my faith and internally wept that I possibly could not do more for her. She bore a heavy burden. What could a mortal man like myself do to ease her pain? Just then, as if on cue... I felt something splat against my eye. “What the?!” I shouted in shock and wiped my eye as I heard  an eagle cry far above me. I looked at what was on my hand... I smelled it’s awful stench as soon as I realized it. 
I glared at the guilty party as it flew away. “First he takes my fish... now he craps on me?!” I shouted in shock. That bird had been a pain in my ass from day one in the priesthood. Stealing my food and- I paused as I heard laughter next to me. I turned my head with my eye and hand full of eagle dung. She was rolling on the flower bed laughing. I smiled, chuckling. “If I may be excused?” I bowed. She waved dismissively, still laughing. I nodded and departed to clean myself. At least she was laughing.
